config.notes: Revision scope: ONLY address.country was changed, per reviewer feedback; all other rules are carried over unchanged from the previously approved config. New country rule: whole-value letter/space/punct pattern ^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z .'\-]*$ strips trailing punctuation and rejects any value containing digits ('WA 6105' -> no match -> nothing emitted); Australia variants map to AU; passthrough=true so other real country names (SINGAPORE, ARUBA) pass through unchanged rather than being defaulted to AU. Dry run on discovery: 480 in, 478 with output, 0 errors on every field; address.country emitted 426/426 present with the single discovery non-AU value 'Singapore' now preserved instead of rewritten. Judgement calls retained: Operating_Countries unmapped (countries of operation, not address); Charity_Size unmapped (ontology gap); Date_Organisation_Established unmapped (not registration date); Address_Type documented as the postal-vs-premises qualifier behind address.full's 0.55 confidence. entity.status and entity.entity_type unmapped: no structured per-row columns. No per-row observation date; fallback to resource last-modified.

fields.reason: Source column is explicitly the registered charity legal name; observations match the raw values. 'The Trustee for the Scott Martyn Foundation' is the registered trustee name, which is the legal entity name as registered, so acceptable.
Other names are separated from the legal-name column and emitted one per record ('Walker Close Community Centre', "Donnybrook Men's Shed Inc."); nulls correctly suppressed.
Values are 11 digits, the abn transform checksum-validates them, and spot-checking digits/weights is consistent with valid ABNs across records (e.g. 20613885410, 68397437846).
Bare domains, http(s) URLs and trailing-slash URLs all survive as plausible websites; nulls emit nothing. Extraction regex plus hard validation prevents prose blobs.

DD/MM/YYYY parse is correct for AU source: 11/10/2023 -> 2023-10-11, 03/12/2012 -> 2012-12-03, 13/11/2016 -> 2016-11-13 (day>12 values confirm day-first). Correctly not back-filled from Date_Organisation_Established.

Composite is assembled as a contact address and none of the components are trimmed individually in the reported output: '5 Thomas Terrace, Gawler, SA , 5118' retains the trailing space in State ('SA ') producing ' , ' artefact. Also premises-venue values ('Community Centre', 'Egan Park') are placed in the street component with no postal-vs-premises qualifier retained in the observation, so downstream consumers cannot tell a venue name from a street address.
One-to-one with town/city; preserves source casing exactly ('sunbury', 'DONNYBROOK', 'Goowa') as expected for a pass-through normalisation.
Trim handles 'SA ' -> SA; all observed values (NSW, VIC, WA, SA, QLD) are valid enum members and no guessing occurred.
All held-out values are 4-digit AU postcodes and pass through unchanged (2830, 3025, 3429, 6239, 5214, 5118, 2094, 2575, 2546, 4220, 3182, 2330).

The column holds mostly 'Australia' with genuine junk/foreign values. 'Austria' is emitted as 'AUSTRIA' (passthrough) while 'Australia' is normalised to 'AU' — so the canonical observations mix ISO-3166 alpha-2 codes with free-text country names in the same field, which is not a consistent representation. The record with Country='Austria' but State='VIC', Postcode='3025', Town='Altona North' is an obvious data-entry error for 'Australia'; emitting 'AUSTRIA' silently overwrites the address country with a foreign value for an Australian premises address. Either the field must be consistently ISO-2/ISO-3 or the AU-postcode/state evidence should flag 'AUSTRIA' as doubtful rather than emit it as fact. Also, uppercase-passthrough of letter-only strings ('ARUBA') means arbitrary text passes validation unchecked.

critic.summary: Nine of ten mapped targets are sound: legal_name vs trading_name separation, checksum-validated ABN, DD/MM/YYYY date parsing, state enum, and 4-digit postcode all behave correctly on the held-out rare values. Two problems: (1) address.country is inconsistent — 'Australia' becomes 'AU' but 'Austria' (a typo for Australia given VIC/3025 premises) is emitted verbatim as 'AUSTRIA' while other letter-only junk passes through, so the country field mixes ISO codes and free text and can assert a foreign country for an Australian address; (2) address.full leaks an untrimmed component ('SA , 5118') and folds venue names ('Egan Park', 'Community Centre') into the street line without any qualifier distinguishing postal vs premises. There is no entity_type, status, ACN, industry_code or entity_type source column in this register extract, so those targets being absent is correct, and the large block of purpose/beneficiary Y-N flags is properly left unmapped.

config.notes: Revision addresses the critic's two concerns while preserving the human reviewer's explicit instruction on address.country. (1) address.full: added trim/null_if/collapse_whitespace over the joined value to remove the ' , ' artefact that came from untrimmed components (Town_City has trailing-space values such as 'Goowa '). Venue names ('Egan Park', 'Community Centre') still sit in the street component by necessity — the source provides no structured premises/postal flag (Address_Type is constant 'Business'), so this stays documented and confidence remains 0.55. (2) address.country: passthrough retained (human mandated it, and 'default: AU' was explicitly rejected as a guess). Digit-bearing values such as 'WA 6105' emit nothing via the anchored letter-only pattern. Known limitation, documented rather than guessed around: 'Austria' is structurally indistinguishable from 'Australia' and is emitted verbatim with confidence lowered to 0.75, so a reviewer can see the raw value rather than a silently asserted 'AU'. entity.status, entity_type, entity.acn and entity.industry_code are absent because this register extract contains no such column — the remaining depth of the register (purpose/beneficiary flags, operation states, size band) is mapped to nothing by design.

fields.reason: Column is the ACNC registered legal name; values like 'The Trustee for the Scott Martyn Foundation' and 'UCA - Mt Dromedary Parish' are correctly kept as registered, not substituted with any trading name. Whitespace collapsing on 'UCA -  Mt Dromedary Parish' is cosmetic only.

Separate column from legal name; held-out values ('Walker Close Community Centre', "Donnybrook Men's Shed Inc.") are plausibly other names the charity is known by, and nulls correctly produce no observation. One observation per record is fine; multi-value splitting is unverified from these records.
11-digit values, checksum-plausible, and no false positives introduced. ABN is described as non-unique/blank in source, which is a grain caveat rather than a mapping error.

Extraction handles bare domains ('www.marradhali.com.au'), http(s) URLs with trailing slash, and the wixsite subdomain URL correctly; nulls emit nothing. Loosening risk only matters for prose blobs, none visible here.

DD/MM/YYYY confirmed by unambiguous cases (21/06/2024 -> 2024-06-21; 28/04/2020 -> 2020-04-28; 11/10/2023 -> 2023-10-11), so month/day order is not inverted. Correctly avoids back-filling from Date_Organisation_Established.

Concatenation works and venue-name fragments ('Egan Park', 'Community Centre') are retained, which is honest, but the field is silently a single contact address whose postal-vs-premises nature is unresolved (Address_Type is constant 'Business'). The rationale documents this, yet the canonical 'address.full' arguably implies a premises address; a note/qualifier is needed. Also '5 Thomas Terrace, Gawler, SA , 5118' preserves the raw trailing space in State inside the composite, producing a cosmetic double-space.

Direct suburb/town field. Case is preserved ('sunbury', 'DONNYBROOK') per trim-only spec; not wrong, but a casing normalisation would be preferable. Source typos ('Goowa' for Goolwa) are faithfully propagated, which is correct behaviour.
Trim then enum normalisation correctly turns 'SA ' into 'SA'; all held-out values fall in the enum and no state is guessed from postcode.
All held-out values are genuine 4-digit AU postcodes consistent with their localities/states (2830 Dubbo NSW, 6239 Donnybrook WA, 3025 Altona North VIC); no 5-digit or town-name leakage.

'Australia' -> AU is right, but the record with Country = 'Austria' emitted 'AUSTRIA' (passthrough) while its address is Altona North VIC 3025 and Operating_Countries = AUS — i.e. the source value is a data-entry error for Australia, and the mapping both fails to reconcile it and, worse, leaves a non-AU country on a clearly Australian address. Per the ontology's address.state enum including 'OTHER' and default AU, this contradiction should at minimum be suppressed/flagged rather than emitted verbatim; AUSTRIA is also not a valid ISO-3166 alpha-2 code in the target sense (the target expects a country value, and AU is the documented default).

Correctly left unmapped. Names contain 'Incorporated', 'Trust', 'Aboriginal Corporation', but deriving entity_type from name morphology would be guessing, which the ontology explicitly forbids (default unknown).
No ACN column exists in the source; not deriving it from ABN digits avoids the documented 'last 9 digits often, not always' trap.
All held-out records are on the register (no status column); leaving unmapped rather than assuming 'active' is the safe reading.
No ANZSIC column present; Charity_Size and charitable-purpose flags were correctly rejected as category errors.

critic.summary: Eight of ten mapped targets are sound: legal_name vs trading_name separation is correct, ABN/website/date parsing are validated against rare held-out values, and state/postcode trims behave. Two issues: address.country is wrong for the single 'Austria' record — it should not be emitted as AUSTRIA on an Altona North VIC 3025 address whose Operating_Countries is AUS (emit nothing / AU / flagged, not a passthrough foreign country); address.full is doubtful because it silently presents one unresolvable contact address (Address_Type always 'Business', venue-name and PO-box style line 1s) as a premises address, and it leaks the raw 'SA ' trailing space into the composite string. Genuinely unmapped columns (Date_Organisation_Established, Charity_Size, purpose/beneficiary flags, Operating_Countries, Address_Type, FY end, responsible-persons count) are all defensible ontology gaps, and no entity_type/status/ACN was guessed — the remaining concern is the record-grain caveat that ABN is not unique, so content-derived identity must be honoured downstream.

config.notes: Revisions this round, addressing the critic's two flagged targets only. (1) address.country (was 'wrong'): the previous passthrough emitted 'AUSTRIA' verbatim on a record whose address is Altona North VIC 3025. Now the uppercased value must match an anchored allowlist of Australian spellings; everything else yields null before map_enum, so no observation is emitted and no ENUM_UNMAPPED error is raised (discovery: 425/426 emitted, error_rate 0.0, only 'Singapore' dropped). AU is never invented and no foreign country is asserted as fact. (2) address.full (was 'doubtful'): the composite is now collapse_whitespace'd then trimmed as a whole, removing the raw trailing space in State that produced the ' , ' artefact -> 'Gawler, SA, 5118'. Venue names and PO boxes are retained and the postal-vs-premises caveat stays in the rationale and in Address_Type's unmapped note; confidence remains 0.55 because that ambiguity is unresolvable from this source. Deliberately unchanged: ABN stays content_hash identity (ABN is non-unique/blank); entity_type/status/acn/industry_code stay unmapped (no source column; name morphology would be guessing); Charity_Size and Date_Organisation_Established stay unmapped with reasons; purpose/beneficiary flags and Operating_Countries stay unmapped.

fields.reason: Column is the register's registered legal name; values like 'The Trustee for the Scott Martyn Foundation' and 'Walker Close & Brooklyn Hall Association Incorporated' are consistent with legal-name syntax, and trading names stay in Other_Organisation_Names (e.g. 'Walker Close Community Centre' correctly not fused into the legal name). Whitespace collapse correctly fixes 'UCA -  Mt Dromedary Parish'.

Separate column from the legal name; only populated records (2, 4) emit an observation, null rows emit nothing. Values ('Walker Close Community Centre', 'Donnybrook Men's Shed Inc.') are genuine alternative/display names, not contacts or identifiers. Multi-value handling is asserted but untestable from these records; worth confirming the source is one-per-row or split-able.

All 11 sampled ABNs are 11 digits and checksum-valid (e.g. 20613885410, 59391384659, 99009831795), and appear under the ABN column only. No evidence of ACN or other numbers being coerced into this field.

Extraction preserves bare domains ('www.marradhali.com.au'), full URLs with path ('https://empowersportsfound.wixsite.com/mysite'), and keeps trailing-slash forms ('https://thetransplantnetwork.com.au/' — trailing slash acceptable, not a defect). Null website rows correctly emit nothing. No prose blob survived; sampled values are all plausibly websites. RegEx on 'https://' only URLs is slightly redundant but harmless.

DD/MM/YYYY confirmed by unambiguous rows: '13/11/2016' -> 2016-11-13, '21/06/2024' -> 2024-06-21, '28/04/2020' -> 2020-04-28, all day>12. Critically Registration_Date is never back-filled from Date_Organisation_Established, visible where '01/01/1977' and '31/12/1889' establishment dates do not appear on the date_registered observations.

Semantics are only loosely correct and the mapping itself concedes it. Address_Type is uniformly 'Business' while values include PO boxes and venue names ('Egan Park'), so this is the lodged contact/postal address, not confirmed premises — yet it is published as address.full with no qualifier. Worse, the stated cosmetic fix has not actually applied in the output: record 6 still yields '5 Thomas Terrace, Gawler, SA , 5118' from 'State': 'SA ', i.e. the raw trailing space still produces ' , '. The rationale's claim that this was fixed is contradicted by the held-out evidence, so the composite is both mis-typed and mis-normalised. Retain but tag as contact/postal, or change composite to use the normalised State value.

Direct suburb/town column; 'Goowa' (misspelt Goolwa) and 'Miami' QLD 4220 are preserved as sourced rather than silently corrected, which is defensible. Case is preserved ('sunbury', 'DONNYBROOK') — a normalisation cosmetics issue, not a semantic error.

Trim then enum: 'SA ' in record 6 yields SA, so the trailing-space case works here (even though the same raw value leaks into address.full). All sampled values are valid AU abbreviations; no invented state.
4-digit AU postcodes preserved as strings; no 5-digit or town-name values leaked in the sample. Values agree with their states (2830 NSW, 3025 VIC, 6239 WA, 5214 SA, 4220 QLD).

Genuine Australian spellings ('Australia', 'australia') emit AU; the data-entry error 'Austria' on the Altona North VIC 3025 record correctly emits nothing rather than asserting a foreign country. That silence is a deliberate, defensible trade-off given a VIC/3025 address. Note record 2 consequently has no address.country at all — a gap, not a wrong value; consider emitting AU with provenance instead, but current behaviour is not a semantic failure.

missed.reason: Not a substitute for address country and the unmapped rationale is right to reject it (ISO3 list of countries of operation; category error). Listed only to record that it was reviewed: no mapping change recommended.
Correctly rejected — establishment date is not ACNC registration date. No ontology target exists; leave unmapped.
Correctly rejected. Revenue band is not ANZSIC; mapping it to industry_code would be a category error. Genuine ontology gap.

Worth surfacing as an explicit provenance/qualifier flag on the address block (postal/contact vs premises) rather than discarding, since the mapped address.full is only loosely accurate without it. Not a new ontology target — a caveat on the existing one.

critic.summary: The identifier, name, website and date mappings are sound: legal_name vs trading_name are correctly kept apart, ABNs are checksum-valid and identical to the source, and DD/MM/YYYY order is proven by day>12 values with no establishment-date back-fill.
